docSummary: Synthetic fixture: four meeting sessions scope one AMS tower covering 12 Agency X eServices (Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave and Claims, Retail, Posting), sized from a FY25 (April 2025-31 March 2026, i.e. 12 months) summary table. Incidents are the Sev A/B/C counts (155/474/7, total 636) mapped to P1/P2/P3 = 24.37%/74.53%/1.10% (P4=0), giving ≈53 incidents/month; SR total 3066/12≈255.5/month; CR total 202/12≈16.83/month - all converted from the stated 12-month FY25 period. Job-failure counters (92 total across services) are operational alerts, not incidents, and were excluded from inc/mix. L1 is out of scope (agency help desk = customer); an L1.5 team filters 20-30% of tickets before L2/L3, and of the remainder <5% reach L3 (used as pass23≈5%; pass12 omitted since L1 is not in the bidder's scope). Two separate manual-automation opportunities were discussed (account review, log analysis), and an AI-generated pod/FTE estimate on page 5 was excluded from extraction as analysis, not client fact.

opportunities.name: Account review automation
opportunities.note: ~12 man-days/month, ~5,000 accounts/month, no central database, manual Excel collation with no audit trail; scope later updated to 12 sources across 5 categories (from an earlier 10 systems).

opportunities.name: Log analysis automation
opportunities.note: Weekly log review, 5 manual use cases, handled by one person via email and Excel workflow.

warnings: Sev A conflict: an earlier session reported platform-wide Sev A = 6 for FY25, but the session-4 table sums Sev A = 155 (dominated by Callup = 140, which looks disproportionate); used the table total of 155 as the most recent explicit figure.
Job-failure counters (Pay=30, Awards=8, Retail=54, Posting=0, total=92) are operational alerts, not logged incidents, and were excluded from inc/mix per instructions.

L1 is explicitly out of scope for the vendor (agency's own help desk) = 'customer'; an L1.5 team of 3-4 people (24x7, manual ticket filtering/routing) is an intermediate team and was treated as context only, not assigned an own tier or used in pass12/pass23 directly.
pass23 (~5%) was derived from 'less than 5% are handled at L3' of the post-L1.5 remainder - treat as an approximate upper bound, not an exact measured rate.
pass12 omitted because L1 sits outside the bidder's scope (handled by the agency's own help desk), per instructions.
incumbentFTE (33) is the midpoint of the stated range '30 to 36 people'; the separately mentioned 18-person platform team was excluded as it is for a separate tender.

eng.region/locMix omitted: the only location detail found is hosting ('public cloud in the Singapore region, run by a separate hosting vendor'), which per instructions is not the bidder's delivery-team location.
Hosting infrastructure (public cloud, Singapore, four environments) is run by a separate hosting vendor and was not sized as an IMS tower, per instructions.

Session 3 states '12 eServices in total; one ("Booklet") is being decommissioned', but the session-4 table lists 12 differently-named eServices with no 'Booklet' row - possible scope/count inconsistency to verify.
Account-review automation scope changed across sessions: '10 systems' (session 1) updated to '12 sources across 5 categories' (session 3); the latest figure was used in opportunities.

A note references obtaining 'six-month manning data' to set a full 12-month baseline, suggesting the Manning row in the FY25 table may itself be based on partial-year data despite FY25 being labelled as a full 12 months - verify against source.
The page-5 'indicative pods / 28 FTE' analysis is explicitly flagged by the document as an AI-generated, non-client-stated estimate and was excluded entirely from extraction, per instructions.

No numeric low/medium/high split was given for CR complexity (only qualitative notes that changes are 'mostly policy driven' and assessment is 'time consuming') - crMix was omitted rather than guessed.
Security incidents are explicitly handled by a separate enterprise team and were excluded from the AMS tower's scope.
Dynatrace monitoring and manual Excel-based tech-debt tracking are mentioned but ownership is not clearly stated as vendor-run, so no IMS tower was created for them.
